summary: In this study, we revisit three widely used techniques in vector search and utilize them to optimize vector embedding indexing through clustering: dimensionality reduction, quantization, and dimension pruning. We propose an indexing pipeline in which these techniques are applied before clustering, and we focus on how they affect storage footprint, clustering time, and the quality of the resulting centroids for vector search tasks. Our results reveal that using full-precision vectors for clustering is excessive, as even 1-bit codes can achieve near-optimal clustering quality (within 1% of ideal) while reducing storage requirements by 60x and delivering attractive performance gains (Figure 1). We open-source our implementations at https://github.com/cwida/SuperKMeans.
core_methodology: The paper revisits clustering techniques for vector embeddings, focusing on dimensionality reduction, quantization, and dimension pruning to optimize vector search tasks. The proposed pipeline reduces storage footprint and clustering time while maintaining near-optimal clustering quality.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but the methodology can be applied to any vector embeddings, including those derived from financial time series or alternative data.
alpha_potential: The techniques could enhance the efficiency of clustering-based trading strategies, such as portfolio construction or anomaly detection, by reducing computational overhead and improving scalability without significant loss in quality.
title_cn: 停止全精度索引：重新审视向量嵌入的聚类方法
summary_cn: 本研究重新审视了向量搜索中的三种常用技术（降维、量化和维度修剪），提出了一种在聚类前应用这些技术的索引管道。结果表明，使用全精度向量进行聚类是过度的，1位编码可实现接近最优的聚类质量（与理想值相差1%），同时减少60倍的存储需求。这一方法可提升金融数据聚类策略的效率和扩展性。

title: The Quantum Shortcut: Complex Phase-State Dynamics Reduce the Optimization Steps of Sequence Models
summary: Sequence models are conventionally distinguished by their backbone, the mechanism that routes information across positions, such as attention or recurrence. This paper varies a choice that is prior to the backbone and shared by nearly all current models: the \emph{substrate}, the number system in which the hidden state is represented together with the form of the map from state to prediction. The prevailing substrate is a real-valued state with an affine--softmax readout; we study a complex-valued alternative drawn from the mathematics of quantum theory, in which information is carried by the phases of the state and scores are quadratic Born forms. Prior work proved an idealized version of this substrate representationally stronger than any real model with a linear readout; we ask whether it also trains faster. Relaxing the two properties that block deployment, exact unitarity and the Born vocabulary readout, we instantiate it in the Mamba state-space model and an attention-based Transformer. At 253M parameters, matched to within $0.02\%$ and trained under one fixed protocol on three byte-level corpora, the complex models reach every measured validation loss in approximately one third (state-space) and one half (attention) of the optimization steps of their real counterparts. The two backbones then diverge. Once the learning-rate warmup ends, the state-space advantage continues to widen, from $0.321$ to $0.354$ bits per character on OpenWebText and from $0.368$ to $0.396$ on FineWeb, which an artifact of the warmup ramp would not do; the attention advantage instead decays toward zero on every corpus, and is therefore an effect of early training.
core_methodology: The paper explores the use of complex-valued states inspired by quantum theory in sequence models, specifically comparing them to traditional real-valued states. It focuses on the training efficiency and performance of these models in sequence prediction tasks.
data_sources: The study uses three byte-level corpora, including OpenWebText and FineWeb, which are general text datasets.
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially be adapted to improve the efficiency of sequence models used in financial time series prediction or natural language processing tasks related to financial data, such as sentiment analysis or news event extraction.
title_cn: 量子捷径：复杂相位状态动力学减少序列模型的优化步骤
summary_cn: 该论文研究了受量子理论启发的复数状态在序列模型中的应用，与传统实数状态相比，训练效率更高。该方法可能适用于金融时间序列预测或与金融数据相关的自然语言处理任务，如情绪分析或新闻事件提取。

title: Semantic Uncertainty-Guided Orchestration in Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems
summary: As large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems become increasingly capable, coordinating agents under uncertainty becomes a fundamental challenge. Existing orchestration strategies typically rely on fixed interaction patterns and often lack mechanisms for assessing the reliability of intermediate reasoning steps, allowing errors and hallucinations to propagate through the system. This paper introduces a semantic-uncertainty-guided orchestration approach, HASSUM as a general framework for uncertainty-aware coordination in multi-agent systems. The method estimates uncertainty using semantic entropy and semantic density, which measure trust at the level of answer semantics rather than output probabilities. These signals enable adaptive orchestration decisions, including output verification, selective reprompting, additional deliberation, and confidence-aware response selection. Because the approach operates independently of any particular agent architecture, it can be integrated into a broad range of hierarchical and collaborative multi-agent systems. The evaluations demonstrate an implementation within a hierarchical agent framework and evaluate it on StrategyQA, JailbreakBench, and TruthfulQA benchmarks. Across tasks that require complex reasoning and are prone to ambiguity or hallucinations, uncertainty-guided orchestration yields more reliable outcomes than uncertainty-unaware coordination. Semantic entropy and semantic density in tandem outperformed either metric alone. Ablations testing different thresholds and model sizes demonstrated that both influence the effectiveness of semantic metrics. The results suggest that semantic uncertainty is a practical and general-purpose signal for improving robustness and trustworthiness in agentic AI systems.
core_methodology: Semantic-uncertainty-guided orchestration approach for multi-agent systems, using semantic entropy and semantic density to measure trust at the level of answer semantics.
data_sources: Evaluated on StrategyQA, JailbreakBench, and TruthfulQA benchmarks, which involve complex reasoning tasks prone to ambiguity or hallucinations.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve robustness and trustworthiness in AI-driven trading systems by reducing errors and hallucinations in multi-agent decision-making processes.
title_cn: 基于语义不确定性的分层多智能体系统协调方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种基于语义不确定性的多智能体系统协调框架HASSUM，通过语义熵和语义密度评估中间推理步骤的可靠性，适用于需要复杂推理且易产生歧义或幻觉的任务。在量化交易中，该方法可能提升AI驱动系统的决策稳健性，减少错误传播。

title: Generative Learning of Separatrices
summary: The identification and reconstruction of the boundaries separating basins of attraction in multistable, multidimensional dynamical systems presents a fundamental challenge in computational dynamics. These structures govern transition pathways and other important large timescale behavior, yet they remain typically under-sampled since their neighborhood does not get routinely visited during direct simulations. Traditional computational approaches face computational limitations in high-dimensional systems and require a priori knowledge of the dynamical system and its equations. Simplistic sampling methods such as random or uniform sampling of the phase space typically fail to quantitatively approximate separatrices and their structure altogether. We introduce and implement a framework that combines supervised classification with generative modeling to address this challenge. Our approach first trains neural network classifiers on uniformly or randomly sampled initial conditions labeled by their corresponding basins of attraction in the system of interest. Using uncertainty metrics of the trained classifier to quantify decision boundaries, the method then identifies these high uncertainty regions and boundaries of the classifier as preliminary approximate separatrices. Subsequently, score-based generative models are trained specifically on samples from high-uncertainty regions, ultimately generating densities of samples consistent with the empirical density of samples on or close to the manifold that constitutes the separatrix between basins in the sampled region. This approach leverages the complementary strengths of (a) discriminative models for global phase space partitioning and (b) generative models for detailed geometric sampling, resulting in a systematic, iterative, data-driven framework that produces empirically consistent reconstructions of (approximate) separatrix manifolds.
core_methodology: The paper combines supervised classification with generative modeling to identify and reconstruct separatrices in dynamical systems. It uses neural network classifiers to label basins of attraction and then employs score-based generative models to sample high-uncertainty regions, effectively approximating the separatrix manifolds.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify financial data sources, but the methodology could theoretically be applied to market regime detection or phase transitions in financial time series.
alpha_potential: The approach could potentially be adapted to identify regime transitions or critical points in financial markets, which may offer alpha opportunities by anticipating large-scale market movements or structural breaks.
title_cn: 分离面的生成学习
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种结合监督分类与生成模型的方法，用于识别和重建多稳态动力系统中的分离面。该技术可潜在应用于金融市场，识别市场状态转换或结构性断裂点，为量化交易提供新的信号来源。

title: BRAID: Learning Equilibrium Maps in Interdependent Security Games via Weight-Tied Iterative Graph Neural Networks
summary: Computing Nash equilibria in interdependent security (IDS) games on networks is computationally expensive: best-response dynamics may need hundreds of iterations per instance, and downstream tasks such as auditing, stress-testing, and incentive design often require repeatedly re-solving the game under parameter perturbations. We propose BRAID, a Best-Response Amortized Iterative Dynamics model that uses a weight-tied iterative graph neural network to learn a direct map from game parameters to Nash equilibrium effort profiles, replacing iterative best response computation with a single forward pass that is up to 43X faster per instance. BRAID is derived from the best-response fixed-point structure of IDS games: its SUM aggregation reflects additive neighbor coupling, and a weight-tied gated recurrent unit (GRU) mirrors a damped best-response update. The same architecture applies across IDS specifications that vary investment-cost curvature and neighborhood aggregation, including log-linear, quadratic-cost, and log constant-elasticity-of-substitution (CES) utilities. Beyond equilibrium prediction, BRAID also recovers how equilibrium efforts change under perturbations to game parameters, including costs and network edge weights. We make this sensitivity recovery an explicit evaluation target and introduce two training strategies, interior-equilibrium training and input-noise regularization, that improve the local behavior of the learned equilibrium map without using sensitivity labels. Experiments show that BRAID effectively predicts Nash equilibria and recovers equilibrium sensitivities across utility specifications and network sizes.
core_methodology: BRAID uses a weight-tied iterative graph neural network to learn a direct map from game parameters to Nash equilibrium effort profiles, replacing iterative best response computation with a single forward pass.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial market data but focuses on game parameters in interdependent security (IDS) games.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to model strategic interactions in financial markets, such as predicting trader behavior or market equilibrium in high-frequency trading environments.
title_cn: BRAID：通过权重绑定的迭代图神经网络学习相互依赖安全博弈中的均衡映射
summary_cn: BRAID提出了一种基于图神经网络的快速计算纳什均衡的方法，适用于预测金融市场中的战略互动和均衡状态。该方法通过单次前向传递显著提高计算效率，潜在应用于高频交易策略和市场微观结构分析。

title: PathFinder: Joint Decompositions of Linked Multimodal Datasets
summary: Low-rank matrix decompositions can uncover patterns and structure in data and have a number of different applications across many disciplines. Extensions to "joint" low-rank decompositions have been proposed to link datasets from different modalities. While these methods enable the discovery of common patterns across modalities, they require that all the multimodal data share one or more dimensions. We propose a new analysis method, PathFinder, that enables co-analysis of datasets that do not necessarily all share a dimension. The key insight is that as long as pairs or subgroups of matrices do share some dimension, and that there are one or more paths that link across the data matrices, a global joint decomposition can be sought out. This enables the joint estimation of common patterns across different modalities, species, or scales, where a one-to-one mapping across all data along some dimension is not necessarily available. We show that PathFinder is a general umbrella under which many matrix decomposition methods fall as special cases. It can be used to discover common patterns across disparate datasets and to make predictions for missing data or modalities.
core_methodology: PathFinder introduces a method for joint low-rank matrix decompositions of linked multimodal datasets that do not necessarily share all dimensions, enabling the discovery of common patterns and structure across disparate datasets.
data_sources: Multimodal datasets, which could include financial time series, alternative data (e.g., news sentiment, social media), and other non-traditional data sources.
alpha_potential: The methodology could uncover hidden patterns and relationships across different financial datasets, potentially leading to new factor discoveries or improved portfolio optimization. However, the direct application to trading strategies requires further validation and adaptation.
title_cn: 路径发现器：联合分解链接的多模态数据集
summary_cn: PathFinder提出了一种联合低秩矩阵分解方法，用于分析不完全共享维度的多模态数据集，能够发现跨数据集的共同模式。在量化交易中，该方法可用于识别跨市场或跨资产的隐藏因子，为多因子策略和组合优化提供新思路。但需进一步验证其在金融数据上的实际效果。

title: Lipschitz Bandits with Arbitrary Feedback Delays
summary: The Lipschitz bandit problem extends the traditional multi-armed bandit framework to continuous action spaces by assuming that the reward functions satisfy a Lipschitz condition. This work investigates Lipschitz bandits under arbitrary feedback delays, where reward signals are not received immediately upon taking an action but after an arbitrarily chosen delay. We consider both stochastic and adversarial reward settings, proposing an elimination-based algorithm and an EXP3-based algorithm, respectively. For both settings, our algorithms achieve a regret bound of $\tilde{O}\left(T^{\frac{d_z+1}{d_z+2}}+\sqrt{D}\right)$ over a time horizon $T$ with total delay $D$, where the main difference between settings lies in the definition of the zooming dimension $d_z$. Our bounds match existing delay-free regret guarantees for Lipschitz bandits and characterize the additional $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{D})$ impact introduced by feedback delays.
core_methodology: The paper proposes elimination-based and EXP3-based algorithms for Lipschitz bandits with feedback delays, applicable to both stochastic and adversarial reward settings.
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to any continuous action space with delayed feedback; no specific market data mentioned.
alpha_potential: Potential application in algorithmic trading strategies where execution delays exist (e.g., high-frequency trading with latency or portfolio rebalancing with settlement delays). The methodology could help optimize decisions under delayed reward observations.
title_cn: 具有任意反馈延迟的Lipschitz多臂老虎机
summary_cn: 本研究探讨了在连续动作空间中具有任意反馈延迟的Lipschitz多臂老虎机问题，提出了适用于随机和对抗性奖励设置的算法。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于存在执行延迟的场景（如高频交易延迟或投资组合再平衡结算延迟），通过优化延迟反馈下的决策过程潜在提升策略表现。理论结果保持了与无延迟情况相同的遗憾界限，仅增加了与总延迟相关的平方根项影响。

title: Online Convex Optimization with Dueling Feedback
summary: We study online convex optimization with dueling (pairwise comparison) feedback, where the learner observes only a binary preference between two queried points. While dueling feedback is well understood in discrete or stochastic settings, the adversarial convex setting has remained unexplored. We propose a simple reduction that converts dueling feedback into approximate gradients, enabling the use of standard first-order methods. We show that regret guarantees transfer under this reduction, yielding the first results for this setting, including $\mathcal{O}(T^{3/4})$ static, adaptive, and dynamic regret. Under additional structure, we obtain improved rates of $\mathcal{O}(T^{2/3})$ for smooth objectives and $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T \log T})$ for strongly convex functions.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a novel approach to online convex optimization using dueling (pairwise comparison) feedback, which is converted into approximate gradients for first-order methods. This methodology is particularly relevant for scenarios where only relative performance feedback is available, a common situation in financial markets where exact returns are not always observable.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is applicable to any financial data where pairwise comparisons can be made, such as relative performance of assets, strategies, or portfolios.
alpha_potential: This approach could be valuable in portfolio optimization and strategy selection where relative performance metrics are more reliable or available than absolute returns. It may help in identifying superior strategies or assets in a noisy or incomplete data environment, potentially uncovering alpha through more robust comparative analysis.
title_cn: 基于对决反馈的在线凸优化
summary_cn: 该论文研究了一种利用对决（成对比较）反馈进行在线凸优化的方法，适用于金融市场中仅能获得相对性能反馈的场景。通过将反馈转化为近似梯度，该方法可用于策略选择和组合优化，提升在噪声环境中的决策质量。

title: GATTA: Graph Active Learning with Test-Time Augmentation
summary: Test-time augmentation (TTA) has proven effective for improving model robustness and uncertainty estimation in computer vision, yet its application to graph-structured data remains largely unexplored. We introduce GATTA (Graph Active Learning with Test-Time Augmentation), a framework for enhancing active learning by aggregating predictions across multiple augmented views to produce more reliable uncertainty estimates. To address the challenge of label-preserving graph augmentations, GATTA incorporates a consistency-based filtering mechanism that discards augmented views yielding unreliable predictions. We systematically evaluate GATTA across multiple graph datasets, GNN architectures, and acquisition strategies. Our results show that simple uncertainty-based methods, such as Entropy and Least Confidence, benefit most from TTA, achieving performance competitive with more sophisticated and computationally expensive approaches. GATTA generalizes across architectures, outperforms model-side ensemble methods such as MC Dropout. We further show that GATTA scales efficiently with both ensemble size and graph size. Extensive analysis of augmentation types, strengths, and filtering strategies provides practical guidelines for effective deployment. Our findings demonstrate that augmenting simple methods with TTA offers a more efficient path to strong active learning performance than engineering complex acquisition functions, enabling practitioners to achieve competitive results with lower computational overhead and reduced implementation complexity.
core_methodology: GATTA introduces a framework for active learning on graph-structured data by leveraging test-time augmentation (TTA) to improve uncertainty estimation. It uses a consistency-based filtering mechanism to discard unreliable augmented views, enhancing the robustness of predictions.
data_sources: The paper evaluates GATTA on multiple graph datasets, but it does not specifically mention financial or market data. However, the methodology could be adapted to financial graph data such as stock correlation networks or transaction graphs.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to produce more reliable uncertainty estimates could be valuable in quantitative finance for tasks like portfolio optimization or risk assessment, where accurate uncertainty measures are critical. However, the direct application to trading strategies is not explicitly demonstrated.
title_cn: GATTA: 基于测试时增强的图主动学习
summary_cn: GATTA通过测试时增强（TTA）提升图数据主动学习中的不确定性估计，采用一致性过滤机制剔除不可靠的增强视图。虽然未直接应用于金融数据，但其方法可适配股票网络或交易图谱，潜在应用于组合优化或风险模型。

title: FinFraudBench: A Heterogeneous Graph Benchmark for Financial Fraud Detection
summary: The increasing complexity of digital financial systems has reshaped financial fraud detection from isolated transaction classification into relational risk reasoning over interconnected financial entities. This shift has motivated graph-based fraud detection, where models identify fraudulent nodes by exploiting dependencies among customers, cards, merchants, categories, and locations. However, despite rapid progress in graph-based methods, existing public benchmarks remain misaligned with real-world financial systems in two important aspects. First, they often simplify financial ecosystems into homogeneous or single-node-type multi-relational graphs, failing to preserve the multi-entity and multi-relational nature of financial data. Second, they rarely provide large-scale heterogeneous financial graph datasets with realistic operating conditions such as extreme class imbalance and limited label availability, making it difficult to assess the practical effectiveness of current methods. To address these gaps, we present FinFraudBench, a heterogeneous graph benchmark for financial fraud detection. FinFraudBench contains two heterogeneous graph datasets (CreditCard-Fraud and BankTrans-Fraud) with up to 8.99M nodes and 89.23M directed typed edges. Each dataset preserves six financial entity types, fourteen directed edge types, and natural fraud rates that mirror deployment constraints. With these datasets, we establish a standardized evaluation protocol covering both ranking and imbalance-sensitive classification metrics, and evaluate representative baselines. Extensive experiments yield empirical insights into current methods' limitations and suggest promising avenues for future research. FinFraudBench is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/FinFraudBench-B002.
core_methodology: Heterogeneous graph-based fraud detection utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to analyze interconnected financial entities (customers, cards, merchants, etc.) with multiple entity types and directed edge types.
data_sources: Two large-scale datasets (CreditCard-Fraud and BankTrans-Fraud) containing up to 8.99M nodes and 89.23M directed typed edges, preserving six financial entity types and fourteen directed edge types with natural fraud rates.
alpha_potential: Potential to identify fraudulent activities in real-time, which could be adapted for detecting market manipulation or suspicious trading patterns in quantitative finance, though direct alpha generation is not explicitly mentioned.
title_cn: FinFraudBench：用于金融欺诈检测的异构图基准
summary_cn: FinFraudBench提出了一个异构图基准，用于金融欺诈检测，包含两个大规模数据集（CreditCard-Fraud和BankTrans-Fraud），涵盖多种金融实体和关系类型。该方法利用图神经网络（GNN）分析复杂金融关系，可能适用于实时市场操纵检测或异常交易模式识别，但需进一步适配量化交易场景。

title: Shape Operator PCA: Curvature-Aware Projections for Geometric Machine Learning
summary: In this paper, we propose SHOPCA (Shape Operator-based Principal Component Analysis), a novel method for unsupervised metric learning and dimensionality reduction that incorporates differential geometric information into the covariance structure of classical PCA. SHOPCA regularizes the global covariance matrix using the mean shape operator, defined as the average of the absolute local shape operators estimated from the data manifold, steering principal components toward directions of both maximum variance and informative curvature. A single trace-normalized mixing coefficient $\alpha$ controls the regularization, recovering standard PCA at $\alpha = 0$ and a curvature-driven embedding as $\alpha \to \infty$. We further introduce a fully unsupervised criterion for selecting $\alpha$ based on the spectral eigengap of the regularized covariance matrix, maximizing the relative separation between the top-$d$ and remaining eigenvalues without using class labels. We evaluate SHOPCA on more than 50 real-world benchmark datasets, comparing it with PCA, ISOMAP, and UMAP using Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Normalized Mutual Information (NMI), Fowlkes-Mallows index (FM), and V-measure. Results show that SHOPCA consistently improves clustering quality over PCA across a broad range of datasets and surpasses UMAP on small-sample settings, where iterative neighborhood-based manifold estimation can degrade. SHOPCA is computationally tractable, parameter-efficient, and applicable to domains requiring fully unsupervised, geometry-aware dimensionality reduction.
core_methodology: SHOPCA is a curvature-aware dimensionality reduction method that incorporates differential geometric information into PCA by regularizing the global covariance matrix with the mean shape operator. It combines variance maximization with curvature-driven embedding.
data_sources: The method was evaluated on more than 50 real-world benchmark datasets, though none explicitly financial. It is designed to work with general manifold-structured data.
alpha_potential: Potential applications could include extracting non-linear features from financial time series, detecting regime changes in market conditions, or improving clustering of assets based on complex relationships. The curvature-awareness might capture market structure information that linear PCA misses.
title_cn: 形状算子PCA：用于几何机器学习的曲率感知投影
summary_cn: SHOPCA通过将曲率信息融入PCA协方差矩阵，实现了一种无监督的几何感知降维方法。在量化交易中，可用于捕捉市场数据的非线性结构、识别不同市场状态或改进资产聚类，特别适用于小样本下的市场微观结构分析。

title: NeuRoute: Logit-Guided Neural Routing for Billion-Scale Vector Search with Sub-Hour Index Construction
summary: Building approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) indexes at billion scale is often dominated by expensive global clustering or graph construction, making time-to-index a first-order systems concern. We present NeuRoute, a learned hashing index that turns short binary codes into an effective routing primitive for large-scale vector search. NeuRoute trains a lightweight neural network encoder with a selective similarity-preserving objective to produce well-balanced binary addresses. During construction, NeuRoute organizes vectors into buckets by their codes and performs bucket-local clustering in the encoder's low-dimensional space to form centroids. At query time, NeuRoute exploits the encoder logits as an uncertainty signal: it uses deviation-to-threshold scores to prioritize uncertain-bit perturbations for query-adaptive multi-bucket probing, scores bucket-local centroids by their distances to the query to form a compact candidate cluster set, and applies centroid-stage gating with heap-quality-driven early stopping to prune low-value clusters before exact refinement. On billion-scale benchmarks, NeuRoute achieves strong accuracy-throughput trade-offs with fast index construction: on BigANN-1B it reaches $90.3\%$ Recall@10 at 2,414 QPS and is $1.7\times$ faster than OPQ+IVF-PQ (refine) at comparable accuracy, while completing end-to-end training+construction in under an hour on both BigANN-1B and Deep1B-1B. These results show that logit-guided neural routing can make hashing competitive as a lightweight ANN indexing framework at billion scale. Source code and artifacts are available at https://github.com/XingqiaoWang/NeuRoute.
core_methodology: Learned hashing index with neural network encoder for efficient vector search, utilizing binary codes for routing and local clustering for nearest neighbor search.
data_sources: Large-scale vector datasets (e.g., BigANN-1B, Deep1B-1B), which could be analogous to high-dimensional financial data such as factor embeddings or time-series representations.
alpha_potential: Potential application in high-dimensional financial data retrieval, such as factor investing or portfolio optimization, where rapid nearest neighbor search could enhance signal extraction or risk management.

title: Not All Attention Is Equal: A Quantitative Survey of the EEI Trade-off
summary: Attention mechanisms have driven machine learning for a decade, from neural machine translation to language models that do general-purpose reasoning. This survey covers four connected threads: their formulation for sequence-to-sequence tasks, adaptation to computer vision, efficiency innovations that address the quadratic bottleneck, and advances in interpretability. We define three criteria: efficiency, expressiveness, and interpretability, and compare twenty-one methods using an EEI scoring framework. Scores come from a single rater with an assumed +/-1-point perturbation range. A deterministic Monte Carlo analysis with 200,000 samples shows that, under this perturbation model, rank changes of more than one position occur in 67-70% of samples on average. A rank-matched null model reproduces a similar stability profile, so the results support coarse tier-level comparisons rather than fine-grained rankings. The survey traces attention from Bahdanau-Luong alignment through the Transformer and into vision architectures. It reviews fixed and learned sparse attention, linear attention, IO-aware exact algorithms including FlashAttention, and state-space alternatives including Mamba. It also covers induction heads, superposition, and the attention-SSM duality. We further provide a structured narrative review, a benchmark synthesis with cross-study caveats, a five-problem research gap analysis, and a 2015-2026 evolution timeline. We conclude by framing attention research as an expansion of the efficiency-expressiveness-interpretability frontier and identifying future directions including unified efficiency benchmarks, learned routing for hybrid architectures, length generalization, and scalable mechanistic interpretability.
core_methodology: The paper presents a comprehensive survey of attention mechanisms in machine learning, focusing on their efficiency, expressiveness, and interpretability (EEI). It evaluates various attention-based models, including Transformers, sparse attention, linear attention, and state-space models like Mamba. The methodology involves a scoring framework and a deterministic Monte Carlo analysis to assess the stability of rankings.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial data sources but discusses general machine learning applications that could be adapted to financial time series or alternative data.
alpha_potential: The potential alpha lies in the adaptation of efficient attention mechanisms for processing high-frequency financial data or sequential market information. Improved interpretability could aid in model transparency for regulatory compliance, while efficiency gains could enable real-time trading signal generation.
title_cn: 并非所有注意力都相同：EEI权衡的定量调查
summary_cn: 本研究综述了注意力机制的发展，聚焦效率、表达能力和可解释性（EEI）的权衡。通过定量评估21种方法，提出了适用于序列任务的高效算法，包括FlashAttention和Mamba模型。在量化交易中，这些技术可用于优化高频数据处理或市场序列建模，但需进一步适配金融数据结构。

title: QSMP: finding representative time series subsequences through Quick Shift+Matrix Profile
summary: Finding representative waveforms in long time series has scientific and practical value in many domains, as it enables summarization and visualization of large time series datasets, and downstream tasks like classification and forecasting. We present here QSMP, a method to find representative waveforms in long time series through a density-guided clustering of time series subsequences. Our method makes a novel connection between Quick Shift, a mode-seeking algorithm, and the Matrix Profile, a time series similarity-search data structure, to adapt Quick Shift to the clustering of subsequences in long time series, with a space complexity that is superior to the state-of-the-art method. Our experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that QSMP can be a valuable tool to summarize and visualize long time series by finding representative waveforms.
core_methodology: QSMP combines Quick Shift (a mode-seeking algorithm) with Matrix Profile (a time series similarity-search data structure) to cluster subsequences in long time series, optimizing space complexity.
data_sources: Can be applied to any financial time series data (e.g., stock prices, FX rates, futures) given its generic time series processing capability.
alpha_potential: Potential for identifying recurring patterns in financial time series that could inform momentum or mean-reversion strategies, though paper doesn't specifically test financial applications.
title_cn: QSMP：通过Quick Shift+Matrix Profile寻找代表性时间序列子序列
summary_cn: QSMP提出了一种基于密度引导的时间序列子序列聚类方法，通过结合Quick Shift算法和Matrix Profile数据结构，有效发现金融时间序列中的代表性波形。该方法可用于识别价格/交易量模式，为动量或反转策略提供特征，但需针对市场数据优化参数。其较低空间复杂度适合处理高频金融数据。

title: ATLAS: Scaffold-Free Algorithm Synthesis by LLMs via Embedding-Guided Quality-Diversity Search
summary: Most LLM-based automated algorithm design methods optimize a designated component within a human-specified scaffold, fixing overall organization and component interactions. We present ATLAS, an embedding-guided quality-diversity framework for scaffold-free full-algorithm synthesis in combinatorial optimization. The problem specification supplies objectives and constraints; a minimal I/O interface fixes only instance and solution formats; the LLM chooses and restructures components, interactions, and control flow. This freedom enlarges the search space, risking invalid candidates and premature convergence to one design region. ATLAS independently detects execution, interface, and feasibility failures, recomputes objectives, and applies error-conditioned repair; similarity-based archive management preserves algorithms across embedding-space regions to counter premature convergence. Its three-layer search refines the best design, gives other regions dedicated refinement opportunities, and performs cross-region synthesis to recombine components and their interactions. Across four NP-hard problems, ATLAS outperforms several state-of-the-art component-synthesis methods and a matched full-synthesis baseline while remaining competitive with strong human-designed algorithms. One ATLAS run retains several algorithms with comparable performance from distinct embedding-space regions rather than a single design. Code inspection finds that these multi-component designs differ in their primary construction or global-search backbone. Our results suggest that embedding-guided quality-diversity search can make the enlarged full-algorithm design space practically searchable. Source code and exact executable prompts are available at https://github.com/Danial-Yazdani/ATLAS .
core_methodology: Embedding-guided quality-diversity framework for scaffold-free full-algorithm synthesis in combinatorial optimization, leveraging LLMs for component and control flow selection.
data_sources: Not specified explicitly, but the methodology can be applied to financial data for combinatorial optimization problems.
alpha_potential: Potential in portfolio optimization and arbitrage strategies by synthesizing novel algorithms tailored to financial combinatorial problems.

title: Amortised Post-Hoc Explanation with Exact Preservation for Dynamic Graph Anomaly Detectors
summary: Anomaly detection in dynamic graphs underpins financial fraud analysis, intrusion detection, and platform integrity, where automated decisions require human-interpretable justifications. StrGNN, the strongest performer in recent benchmarks, produces no explanation: when an edge is flagged, the analyst receives only a score. Explanation metrics are undefined for StrGNN because no attribution vector exists. This paper closes that gap. We present X-StrGNN, a post-hoc explanation layer that wraps a trained, frozen StrGNN and emits, for every flagged edge, dual attributions: a structural attribution identifying which contextual interactions in the enclosing subgraph drove the decision, and a temporal attribution identifying which historical snapshot carried the signal. Both attributions are multiplicative masks identically one in the unexplained pass, so the layer is an exact pass-through: detection is preserved to machine precision, verified rather than asserted (Delta AUC = 0.0000, Delta AP = 0.0000, Delta P@100 = 0.0000). Attribution costs 0.66 ms per edge, making explanation of an entire alarm list feasible. We conduct the first controlled design study of attribution strategies for this architecture, comparing gradient attribution, per-instance mask optimisation, and amortised parameterisation under one protocol, one budget, and three seeds. X-StrGNN attains the highest stability (0.913) at 268x lower cost than per-instance optimisation, and its temporal attribution (1.601 against a measured random floor of 0.973) is separably better than its ablated control, while per-instance optimisation - the most expensive strategy - falls below that floor. Code, protocol, and per-seed measurements are released.
core_methodology: X-StrGNN is a post-hoc explanation layer for StrGNN, providing dual attributions (structural and temporal) for anomaly detection in dynamic graphs. It uses multiplicative masks to ensure exact preservation of detection performance while adding explainability.
data_sources: Dynamic graphs, likely including financial transaction networks or interaction data relevant to fraud detection.
alpha_potential: The method could identify hidden patterns in financial transaction networks, potentially uncovering fraudulent activities or anomalous trading behaviors that are not easily detectable by traditional methods.
title_cn: 动态图异常检测器的精确保真事后解释摊销方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出X-StrGNN，一种为动态图异常检测器StrGNN添加事后解释功能的层，能精确保持原模型性能的同时提供结构和时间上的归因解释。这对于金融欺诈检测等场景有应用潜力，可帮助分析人员理解异常交易背后的模式，但需适配金融数据特性。

title: Large Discovery Models: Empirically-grounded Model-Based Open-Ended Search
summary: Scientific discovery often involves optimising expensive-to-evaluate objectives over vast, structured, and open-ended hypothesis spaces, such as molecules, protein sequences, and computer programs. Generative models such as large language models (LLMs) provide expressive priors over such spaces, but their likelihoods and self-assessments are unreliable proxies for the objectives and calibrated epistemic uncertainty, especially for novel candidates outside the observed data distribution. We introduce the Large Discovery Model (LDM), an empirically grounded recurrent architecture that couples a generative model with a Bayesian non-parametric reward surrogate model. The generative model proposes and refines candidate designs, while the surrogate predicts their performance and quantifies uncertainty, yielding an uncertainty-aware value that guides candidate generation, refinement, and selection. The discovery memory and the surrogate model are continually updated as each new experimental observation arrives. We evaluate LDM on three scenarios spanning different design modalities and objectives, including neural-network training, antibody design, and molecular optimisation. Compared to LLM-only reflection or traditional statistical search across these domains, LDM achieves a $2.4\times$ greater reduction in validation BPB, an $18.2\%$ relative decrease in binding energy, and more than $60\%$ relative gains in molecular multi-objective performance. These results suggests that LDM could serve as a general-purpose discovery engine for effective search over open-ended hypothesis spaces.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the Large Discovery Model (LDM), which combines a generative model with a Bayesian non-parametric reward surrogate model. The generative model proposes and refines candidate designs, while the surrogate predicts their performance and quantifies uncertainty, guiding candidate generation and selection. This methodology is designed for open-ended search in complex hypothesis spaces.
data_sources: The paper evaluates LDM on scenarios including neural-network training, antibody design, and molecular optimisation, but does not specify financial data sources. However, the methodology could potentially be adapted to financial data for tasks like portfolio optimisation or algorithmic strategy discovery.
alpha_potential: The LDM's ability to explore open-ended hypothesis spaces with uncertainty quantification could be adapted to discover novel trading strategies or optimise portfolio allocations. The uncertainty-aware value guidance might help in identifying robust strategies that perform well out-of-sample.
title_cn: 大型发现模型：基于经验的开放式搜索模型
summary_cn: 该论文提出的大型发现模型（LDM）结合生成模型和贝叶斯非参数奖励代理模型，用于开放式假设空间的探索。虽然论文未涉及金融数据，但其方法可潜在应用于量化交易领域，如策略发现和组合优化，尤其擅长度量不确定性以增强策略稳健性。

title: Adaptive Mixing of Policies from Searching and Policies from Learning
summary: Background: Distillation of training targets generated thru search/planning has proven useful in reinforcement learning, but search can take exceedingly long. Objectives: Rather than perform search to the same depth every time (typically at a fixed period of steps), reduce the search depth proportionally to the quality of the policy network priors. Methods: We describe Flexer, an architecture that, for each step, mixes the policy from a neural network and the policy from Monte Carlo tree search. The mixing factor favors the MCTS policy as the policy imitation error of the network and the environment models' variance increases. Results: Flexer outperforms a version of AlphaZero (and DQN and ADP) for some experiments on three toy symbolic problems.
core_methodology: Flexer is an architecture that mixes the policy from a neural network and the policy from Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS). The mixing factor is dynamically adjusted based on the policy imitation error of the network and the environment models' variance.
data_sources: The paper experiments on three toy symbolic problems, not directly involving financial markets. However, the methodology could potentially be adapted for trading strategies.
alpha_potential: The dynamic mixing of policies could enhance trading strategy robustness by combining learned behaviors with search-based strategies (e.g., backtested or simulated strategies).
title_cn: 策略的自适应混合：来自搜索的策略与来自学习的策略
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种名为Flexer的架构，动态混合神经网络策略与蒙特卡洛树搜索(MCTS)策略。这种自适应混合方法可以增强策略的稳健性，适用于交易策略中结合学习型与搜索型策略的开发，尤其在需要动态调整的市场环境中潜在应用价值较高。

title: FirstDiff: One-Step Diffusion-Based Anomaly Detection for Multivariate Time Series via Initial Noise Prediction
summary: Diffusion models have recently shown strong potential for multivariate time-series anomaly detection by learning the distribution of normal data through iterative denoising. Existing diffusion-based approaches, however, typically perform anomaly detection after completing the reverse diffusion process, relying primarily on the final reconstructed signal and overlooking informative representations produced during denoising. This design incurs substantial computational cost and limits the use of intermediate diffusion information for anomaly detection. In this paper, we propose FirstDiff, a diffusion-based anomaly detection framework based on the observation that the predicted diffusion noise at the initial reverse-diffusion evaluation already contains sufficient information for accurate anomaly detection. FirstDiff models the statistical distribution of predicted diffusion noise under normal behavior using validation data, enabling anomaly inference from a single denoising-network evaluation rather than completing the reverse diffusion trajectory. To model complex temporal and inter-sensor dependencies, FirstDiff employs a Diffusion Transformer as the denoising backbone. Extensive experiments on five public benchmark datasets demonstrate that FirstDiff achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing diffusion inference from the full reverse trajectory to a single denoising-network evaluation.
core_methodology: FirstDiff uses a diffusion model with a transformer backbone to predict initial diffusion noise for anomaly detection in multivariate time series, reducing computational cost by focusing on a single-step evaluation.
data_sources: Public benchmark datasets (unspecified but likely generic multivariate time series data, not financial markets).
alpha_potential: Potential for detecting anomalous patterns in financial time series (e.g., sudden price movements, volume anomalies) with efficient single-step inference, but requires adaptation to market data.
title_cn: FirstDiff：通过初始噪声预测实现多变量时间序列的一步扩散异常检测
summary_cn: FirstDiff提出了一种基于扩散模型的异常检测方法，首次实现单步评估即可完成检测。其创新点在于仅利用初始扩散噪声的统计分布来识别异常，大幅降低计算成本（相比传统扩散模型需完整逆向扩散）。虽未直接应用于金融数据，但该方法可迁移至高频交易中异常波动检测、多资产联动异常识别等场景，尤其适合实时性要求高的交易系统。

title: Temporal Graph Prototype-conditioned Conformal Prediction for Fraud Detection
summary: Conformal prediction (CP) provides distribution-free coverage guarantees and has emerged as a principled tool for uncertainty quantification. In edge-level fraud detection on temporal interaction graphs, where false positives and false negatives both carry substantial cost, such coverage guarantees are particularly appealing for risk-aware decision making. However, directly applying existing graph conformal predictors yields inefficient prediction sets due to two recurring properties of fraud data. Fraudulent interactions are often embedded in benign-dominated neighborhoods that dilute calibration signals, while extreme class imbalance leaves scarce labeled-fraud support in the calibration split and leads to overly conservative class-conditional thresholds. To address these issues, we propose ProtoCP, a conformal prediction framework for edge-level fraud detection on temporal graphs. ProtoCP improves calibration efficiency by focusing calibration on fraud-relevant subgraph context and producing more stable nonconformity scores under class imbalance and temporal drift. Specifically, it leverages learned prototypes to suppress benign-dominated noise in the calibration context and introduces a neighborhood-relative scoring mechanism with temporal score diffusion for stable class-conditional calibration. Experiments on four fraud benchmarks (YelpChi, S-FFSD, FTFD, and BankSim) show that ProtoCP achieves the target coverage with consistently smaller prediction sets than state-of-the-art baselines. Our codes are available at https://github.com/Picard1701ent/ProtoCP.git
core_methodology: The paper introduces ProtoCP, a conformal prediction framework for edge-level fraud detection on temporal graphs. It leverages learned prototypes to focus calibration on fraud-relevant subgraph context and introduces a neighborhood-relative scoring mechanism with temporal score diffusion for stable class-conditional calibration.
data_sources: The paper uses four fraud benchmarks (YelpChi, S-FFSD, FTFD, and BankSim) for experiments. These datasets likely involve transaction or interaction data with labeled fraudulent activities.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to detect fraudulent activities in financial transactions, such as credit card fraud or market manipulation, providing a risk-aware decision-making tool with distribution-free coverage guarantees.
title_cn: 基于时序图原型条件化的欺诈检测的共形预测
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种基于共形预测的时序图欺诈检测框架ProtoCP，通过关注欺诈相关的子图上下文和引入邻居相对评分机制，提高了校准效率。该方法可用于金融交易中的欺诈检测，如信用卡欺诈或市场操纵，为风险决策提供保障。

title: Governance at the Boundary: How Agent Decomposition Degrades Policy Compliance
summary: Existing agent benchmarks ask whether the agent finished the task. We ask whether it finished it within policy. We introduce Fiducia-bench, a benchmark for the governability of financial agents---whether they escalate when obligated, abstain when required, and leave an auditable trail---and use it to study a question no prior benchmark addresses: does decomposing an agent into components degrade its governance? It does, and the mechanism is specific. Policy-relevant facts discovered by one component are attenuated at the handoff boundary before reaching the component that must act on them. In a 626-episode experiment across 100 KYC/AML task variants, two models, and three architectures, a 32B open-weights model attenuated 0% of discovered facts under a single-loop baseline, 56% under a fixed pipeline, and 85% under an orchestrator-subagent architecture (all at constraint distance 2). A stronger model (gpt-4.1-mini) attenuated 3-6% under the same conditions, suggesting the governance cost of decomposition is partly a function of model capability. Critically, the same mechanism produces both under-escalation and over-escalation, depending on whether the dropped fact was a risk signal or an exculpating one. The benchmark, all tasks, and the verification harness are open-source
core_methodology: The paper introduces Fiducia-bench, a benchmark for evaluating the governability of financial agents, focusing on their ability to comply with policies, escalate when necessary, and maintain auditable trails. It examines how agent decomposition affects policy compliance through experiments across different architectures and models.
data_sources: The study uses synthetic tasks and scenarios related to KYC/AML (Know Your Customer/Anti-Money Laundering) compliance, with experiments conducted across 100 task variants, two models, and three architectures.
alpha_potential: The research highlights the importance of governance in financial agents, which could be applied to automated trading systems to ensure compliance with regulatory and internal policies. The findings suggest that more capable models (e.g., gpt-4.1-mini) exhibit better governance, which could inform the design of compliant trading algorithms.
title_cn: 边界治理：代理分解如何降低政策合规性
summary_cn: 该论文通过Fiducia-bench基准评估金融代理的治理能力，研究代理分解对政策合规性的影响。实验表明，模型能力越强，治理成本越低。这一发现对设计合规的自动化交易系统具有参考价值。

title: Learn What's Left, Not What's Mastered: Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) with group-relative advantages has become the de facto standard for post-training language model reasoners. However, when optimizing multiple reward objectives, existing methods typically scalarize the reward vector with a fixed weighted sum before group-wise standardization. We show that this design leads to two fundamental problems: rollouts with distinct reward profiles can receive identical advantages, and all objectives are optimized with fixed relative weights regardless of their current level of saturation. As a result, training continues to allocate gradient budget to already-solved objectives instead of focusing on those with greater remaining headroom. We introduce \textbf{Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization} (SA-MRPO), which standardizes each reward objective independently and adaptively discounts its contribution according to a batch-level estimate of objective saturation. This dynamically reallocates optimization effort toward under-optimized objectives while empirically maintaining performance on those that are already well satisfied. We further show that saturation-aware reweighting can reverse the sign of an update, rather than merely rescale its magnitude. Across mathematical reasoning with two- and three-objective reward combinations, SA-MRPO improves the harder correctness objective over GDPO in 12 of 15 benchmark comparisons, with gains of up to $5\%$ on AIME24. On adaptive reasoning it improves accuracy on all five benchmarks, by $3.8\%$ on average and up to $9.2 \%$ on AMC23, and on coding benchmarks it improves pass rate by up to $2.3\%$, while in all settings maintaining the easier objectives near their already satisfied levels.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Saturation Aware Advantage Reweighting for Multi-Reward Policy Optimization (SA-MRPO), which dynamically reweights rewards based on their saturation levels to optimize multiple objectives more effectively in reinforcement learning settings.
data_sources: While the paper focuses on mathematical reasoning and coding benchmarks, the methodology is applicable to any domain with multiple reward objectives, including financial trading where multiple performance metrics (e.g., Sharpe ratio, max drawdown, win rate) need to be optimized.
alpha_potential: The adaptive reweighting of objectives based on their saturation could help in developing trading strategies that dynamically focus on under-optimized performance metrics, potentially leading to more robust and balanced trading algorithms.
title_cn: 学习未掌握的内容，而非已掌握的：面向多奖励策略优化的饱和度感知优势重加权
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种饱和感知的优势重加权方法（SA-MRPO），用于在多奖励强化学习任务中动态调整优化目标，根据当前饱和度重新分配优化资源。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于同时优化多个交易目标（如夏普比率、最大回撤），重点关注尚未达标的指标，从而提升策略的整体平衡性和稳健性。

title: Eigenanalysis framework for autoregressive neural emulators of multi-scale chaotic dynamics
summary: Neural autoregressive models have rapidly emerged as powerful emulators of high-dimensional chaotic systems, yet their long-term instability and error growth remain poorly understood, leading to ad-hoc solutions. Here, we develop an eigenanalysis framework that reveals the dynamical origin of this error growth. By analyzing the Jacobian of the learned one-step update map with respect to the state, we show how inference-time error growth, and thus model stability, is governed by its spectral radius. Direct-step architectures (models that predict the next state from the previous one) generically admit unstable eigenvalues with magnitudes exceeding one, explaining the rapid divergence of these widely used models. In contrast, integration-constrained models (where the time derivative is estimated and integrated with a higher-order integrator) collapse their eigenspectrum onto the unit circle, yielding neutral stability and a universal linear error-scaling law. The largest eigenvalue of this Jacobian provides an architecture-agnostic, a priori diagnostic of short-term skill, long-term stability, and spectral bias, without requiring an expensive rollout. Leveraging this theory, we introduce a stability-promoting loss that explicitly regularizes Jacobian-driven error amplification, improving both forecast accuracy and dynamical robustness. Demonstrated across $29$ models spanning two architectures, several explicit and implicit integrators, and multiple loss functions on the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky system, our results establish a theoretical foundation for the design and evaluation of neural emulators of chaotic multi-scale dynamics. More broadly, our framework is a step toward the kind of a priori stability analysis that numerical analysis provides for discretizations of differential equations and that scientific machine learning currently lacks.
core_methodology: Eigenanalysis of Jacobian matrices in neural autoregressive models to understand and control error growth in chaotic systems, with applications to improving model stability and forecast accuracy.
data_sources: The study uses the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky system, a model for chaotic multi-scale dynamics, which is a theoretical model rather than financial market data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to improve the stability and accuracy of neural network models used in financial time series forecasting, particularly in high-frequency trading where chaotic dynamics are prevalent.

title: When Single-Dataset Conclusions Fail: A 45-Task Study of Threshold Tuning and Resampling for Imbalanced Classification
summary: Class-imbalance handling is routinely evaluated on a single benchmark dataset, and the resulting conclusions are reported as if they were properties of the method. We show this practice is unsafe. On the public Kaggle credit-card fraud dataset, under a leakage-free nested cross-validation protocol in which the decision threshold is selected on a held-out inner validation fold, a plain Random Forest at the default 0.5 threshold attains F1 = 0.861 +/- 0.021, and threshold tuning yields it no benefit (delta-F1 = -0.002). Read alone, this supports an appealing conclusion: for a well-calibrated ensemble, imbalance handling is unnecessary. We then apply the identical protocol to 45 binary tasks spanning imbalance ratios from 1:1.5 to 1:178 (2,025 model fits, four model families). The conclusion reverses. Random Forest benefits most from threshold tuning across the suite (delta-F1 = +0.101 +/- 0.134), not least, while three other families replicate their fraud-dataset behaviour almost exactly. SMOTE likewise harms the fraud dataset but helps across the suite (mean delta-F1 = +0.076; 138 wins, 39 losses; Wilcoxon p = 2.7e-17). Two further results. Threshold-tuning benefit is non-monotonic in the imbalance ratio: near zero below 1:5, peaking at +0.120 in the 1:15-1:40 band, declining to +0.045 beyond 1:100 - explaining why the fraud dataset, at 1:577, is an unrepresentative place to study the question. And we reject an intuitive heuristic: validation-set calibration error does not predict tuning benefit (expected calibration error r = -0.087; Brier r = +0.137), so calibration diagnostics cannot tell a practitioner whether tuning is worthwhile. We release the protocol, the 45-task harness, and all per-run metrics.
core_methodology: The paper investigates the impact of threshold tuning and resampling techniques on imbalanced classification tasks across 45 different datasets, using a leakage-free nested cross-validation protocol. It evaluates four model families, including Random Forest, and measures performance via F1 score.
data_sources: The study uses 45 binary classification tasks with varying imbalance ratios, including the Kaggle credit-card fraud dataset (imbalance ratio 1:577). The datasets span imbalance ratios from 1:1.5 to 1:178.
alpha_potential: The findings suggest that threshold tuning and resampling techniques like SMOTE can significantly improve model performance in imbalanced classification tasks, which could be applied to fraud detection, anomaly detection, or other imbalanced financial datasets (e.g., rare event prediction in trading). The non-monotonic relationship between imbalance ratio and tuning benefit provides actionable insights for model selection in finance.
title_cn: 单一数据集结论的失效：关于阈值调整和重采样在45个不平衡分类任务中的研究
summary_cn: 本文通过45个不平衡分类任务（包括Kaggle信用卡欺诈数据集）研究了阈值调整和重采样技术的影响。研究发现，阈值调整对Random Forest模型效果提升显著（平均ΔF1=+0.101），且SMOTE在大多数任务中有效（平均ΔF1=+0.076）。这些方法可用于金融领域的欺诈检测或罕见事件预测，但效果与不平衡比例呈非线性关系。

title: Understanding and Stabilizing Deep Q-Learning via Controlled Bootstrapping and Regulated Value Dynamics
summary: Deep Q-learning (DQL) has achieved remarkable empirical success in reinforcement learning, yet its training process remains notoriously unstable. Existing studies often attribute instability to isolated factors such as overestimation bias or representation learning issues, lacking a unified understanding of how different sources of instability interact during recursive value estimation. In this work, we provide a systematic analysis of instability in deep Q-learning from three complementary perspectives: operator-level bias in Bellman bootstrapping, estimator-level sensitivity of greedy action selection to regression noise, and parameter-dynamics imbalance under aggressive data reuse. We identify a reward-triggered self-reinforcing trap and characteristic parameter spike dynamics, then derive stabilization principles for controlled bootstrapping, ensemble quantile estimation, and spike-based parameter regulation. Experiments on Atari-100K and Procgen demonstrate competitive performance and improved training stability.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a systematic analysis and stabilization techniques for Deep Q-Learning (DQL), focusing on controlling bootstrapping, ensemble quantile estimation, and parameter regulation to address instability in recursive value estimation.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the methodology on Atari-100K and Procgen environments, which are standard benchmarks in reinforcement learning but not financial datasets. However, the techniques could be adapted to financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The stabilization techniques could improve the robustness of reinforcement learning-based trading strategies, particularly in high-frequency or algorithmic trading where recursive value estimation is critical. The controlled bootstrapping and ensemble methods may help reduce overfitting and improve generalization in financial markets.
title_cn: 通过受控自举和调节值动态理解并稳定深度Q学习
summary_cn: 本研究通过系统性分析深度Q学习中的不稳定因素，提出了受控自举、集成分位数估计和基于尖峰的参数调节等稳定技术。这些方法可增强强化学习在量化交易中的鲁棒性，特别是在高频交易中递归价值估计的稳定性，具有潜在的应用价值。

title: Multi-Granularity Sentiment Integration for LLM-Based Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
summary: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to predict sentiment polarity and intensity from heterogeneous inputs such as text, audio, and vision. While large language models (LLMs) offer strong semantic priors for MSA, effectively incorporating audio and visual signals effectively remains challenging. A key challenge is that audio and visual sentiment cues evolve over different temporal scales, yet many LLM-based methods compress these signals through shallow projection or coarse pooling before fusing them with text, which can weaken cross-modal alignment and erase fine-grained affective information. We propose MGSI, a multi-granularity sentiment integration framework for LLM-based MSA. MGSI first encodes audio and visual streams at short-, medium-, and long-range temporal scales, preserving both local variations and global affective trends. It then refines non-text features through text-guided alignment, and applies polarity- and intensity-aware enhancement to better handle ambiguous and near-neutral samples. The resulting multimodal representation is finally compressed into a small set of pseudo-tokens for efficient conditioning of a frozen LLM. Experiments on four public benchmarks show that MGSI substantially outperforms frozen-LLM baselines and remains competitive with strong multimodal methods. Further ablation and sensitivity analyses support the effectiveness of multi-granularity temporal modeling, text-guided refinement, and adaptive sentiment calibration.
core_methodology: Multi-granularity sentiment integration framework (MGSI) that encodes audio and visual streams at different temporal scales, refines non-text features through text-guided alignment, and applies polarity- and intensity-aware enhancement for multimodal sentiment analysis.
data_sources: Heterogeneous inputs such as text, audio, and vision from public benchmarks (specific datasets not mentioned).
alpha_potential: Potential to enhance sentiment analysis in financial markets by integrating multimodal data (e.g., earnings call transcripts, audio tones, and visual cues from executive presentations) to improve sentiment-driven trading strategies.
title_cn: 基于大语言模型的多模态情感分析的多粒度情感整合
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种多粒度情感整合框架（MGSI），用于基于大语言模型的多模态情感分析。通过在不同时间尺度上编码音频和视觉流，并结合文本引导的对齐和情感校准，该方法可提升金融场景（如财报电话会议）中的多模态情感分析能力，为情感驱动交易策略提供潜在信号源。

title: Efficient Coreset Selection via K-Nearest Neighbor Graphs
summary: Coreset selection reduces the cost of model training by replacing a large training set with a small representative subset. Existing gradient-approximation coreset methods such as CRAIG and cluster-based variants can preserve model accuracy. Still, their selection stages often rely on dense pairwise distances or large item-cluster bound matrices, leading to high time and memory costs on large datasets. This paper proposes KNNG-CS, a lightweight coreset selection method based on a $K$-nearest neighbor graph. KNNG-CS exploits local neighborhood structures to estimate the importance of each data item and greedily selects representative nodes without maintaining a quadratic distance matrix. The method requires only linear storage in the number of edges. Experiments on four real-world datasets show that KNNG-CS achieves accuracy comparable to representative gradient-approximation coreset methods, while reducing selection time by $2.3\times$-$41.2\times$ and peak memory to $0.3\%$-$7.5\%$ of the baselines.
core_methodology: The paper introduces KNNG-CS, a coreset selection method based on K-nearest neighbor graphs, which efficiently selects a representative subset of data for model training while reducing computational overhead. This approach is particularly useful for handling large datasets by leveraging local neighborhood structures for importance estimation.
data_sources: While the paper itself does not specify financial datasets, the methodology can be applied to any large-scale dataset, including financial time series, alternative data, or even preprocessing steps for AI/ML models in trading.
alpha_potential: The proposed method could be useful in financial applications by reducing the computational cost of training models on large datasets, potentially enabling faster iteration on strategy development. It is particularly relevant for scenario analysis, stress testing, or preprocessing steps in AI-driven trading systems where computational efficiency is crucial.
title_cn: 基于K近邻图的高效核心集选择方法
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种基于K近邻图的轻量级核心集选择方法KNNG-CS，通过利用局部邻域结构估计数据项重要性，显著降低了计算和存储成本。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于高频数据处理、策略优化等场景，提升模型训练效率并降低运营成本，尤其适合处理海量金融时间序列数据。

title: Coverage-Maximizing Multinomial Subset Routing under Operational Constraints
summary: We introduce Multinomial Subset Routing (MSR), a new online routing framework over $K$ experts in which the learner keeps a multinomial routing policy instead of a deterministic subset of experts. At each round, the learner samples $M$ experts i.i.d. from the multinomial policy, and the resulting set of distinct sampled experts forms the routed subset. The reward depends only on the best-performing expert(s) in the routed subset. This reward structure arises naturally in routing across specialized models but is not captured by standard combinatorial bandits or subset-selection methods, which optimize deterministic subsets and typically assume additive rewards. We require the selection to satisfy several long-term, two-sided operational constraints under bandit feedback, observing only the winner's reward each round. We propose OMD-Approachability, combining online mirror descent with Blackwell's Approachability, and prove it achieves $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ regret in both reward and constraint violation. We ground the framework in practical application domains and validate it empirically on a real-world crowdsourcing dataset.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Multinomial Subset Routing (MSR), an online routing framework that uses a multinomial routing policy to sample experts. It combines online mirror descent with Blackwell's Approachability to optimize rewards under operational constraints, achieving O(1/√T) regret in both reward and constraint violation.
data_sources: The paper validates the framework on a real-world crowdsourcing dataset, but the methodology could theoretically be applied to financial data such as trading signals or expert predictions.
alpha_potential: The framework could be adapted to dynamically route capital among competing trading strategies or models, optimizing for the best-performing strategy under operational constraints. This could potentially capture alpha by dynamically allocating to the most effective strategies in real-time.
title_cn: 操作约束下的覆盖率最大化多项式子集路由
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种新的在线路由框架（MSR），通过多项式分布动态选择专家子集，优化最佳表现专家的奖励。该方法可应用于量化交易中动态分配资金至不同策略，优化组合表现并满足操作约束。

title: FETERS: Few-Shot Early Time-Series Classification via Effective Ratio Selection
summary: Early time-series classification (ETSC) aims to make accurate predictions from partially observed time series as early as possible. Although various stopping mechanisms and feature learning strategies have been developed for ETSC, most existing methods assume access to sufficient labeled training data, which may be unrealistic in applications with limited annotation. Under limited supervision, learning an additional sample-level stopping module and extracting effective classification features can both become challenging. In this paper, we propose FETERS, a few-shot ETSC framework that selects a dataset-level stopping ratio through class-wise leave-one-out (LOO) evaluation on the support set and uses a penalty-based reward function to manage the accuracy-earliness trade-off, thereby avoiding the need to train an additional stopping module. FETERS further combines Rocket-based features with frozen Chronos representations for classification. Extensive experiments on 69 public datasets spanning 14 domains show that FETERS achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in the 5-shot setting, with the highest average harmonic mean (HM) and the best HM on 38 datasets, while outperforming the current SOTA method on 44 datasets. FETERS also remains competitive in the full-shot setting, demonstrating its effectiveness in managing the accuracy-earliness trade-off.
core_methodology: FETERS combines Rocket-based features with frozen Chronos representations for few-shot early time-series classification, using class-wise leave-one-out evaluation on the support set to select a dataset-level stopping ratio. It employs a penalty-based reward function to manage the accuracy-earliness trade-off, eliminating the need for a sample-level stopping module.
data_sources: Tested on 69 public datasets spanning 14 domains, suggesting potential applicability to financial time-series data, although not explicitly tested on market data in the paper.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to make accurate early predictions with limited data could be valuable for high-frequency trading, early trend detection, or short-term momentum strategies where early identification of patterns is crucial. The accuracy-earliness trade-off management is particularly relevant for algorithmic trading systems.
title_cn: FETERS：基于有效比率选择的少样本早期时间序列分类方法
summary_cn: FETERS通过结合Rocket特征与Chronos表示，在少量样本情况下实现早期时间序列分类。该方法的特点是不需要单独训练停止模块，通过惩罚奖励函数管理准确性与及时性的权衡。这种在数据有限情况下的早期预测能力，对高频交易中的模式识别和趋势预测有潜在应用价值。

title: SoftModel: A Neural Model That Grows Its Own Topology -- Governed Structural Growth for Continual In-Service Learning
summary: Today, a neural system is almost always used in two phases -- trained, then deployed -- and in that regime it freezes twice: training ends, and the topology itself was never a degree of freedom. We take the opposite premise as an axiom -- total plasticity: no part of a model, including its structure, is ever frozen -- and derive the governance a lifelong learner then requires. The design's target regime is continual, in-service learning: a long-lived model on a non-stationary stream, whose stability comes from governance rather than immobility and whose capacity follows demand. The result is a growable soft model: an algebra of structural operators (width, hierarchy, composition, input interface, grown cycles, attention heads), each exact at application, budgeted, and audited, with adoption decided solely by a held-out reality gate that treats parametric and structural change uniformly. A complete from-scratch system realizes the whole account; its factory surface is operated end-to-end by a production LLM. Two conclusions follow from the axiom by construction: stability under lifelong change becomes an audit property of the lifecycle, and structure that follows demand removes the silent cap a fixed topology places on later capability where the capacity floor binds. A third is measured: in the worlds where this was measured, the marginal value of new capacity was unobservable before adoption, so workable growth governance took its ex-post form. The same governance extends to evaluative signals, and the core method is evaluated on standard continual-learning benchmarks, where governed growth preserves the ability to keep learning along long task sequences. A pre-registered experimental program adjudicates the mechanism and value claims on the tested problems and reports its failures at full prominence; the map -- positive and negative -- is the contribution.
core_methodology: A neural model that dynamically grows its own topology to adapt to non-stationary data streams, governed by structural operators and a reality gate for continual learning.
data_sources: Non-stationary data streams, potentially applicable to financial time series or market microstructure data.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to adapt to changing market conditions dynamically could uncover new patterns or inefficiencies that fixed-topology models might miss, especially in volatile or regime-shifting markets.
title_cn: SoftModel：一种自主生长其拓扑结构的神经模型——持续在线学习中的结构生长管理
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种动态生长拓扑结构的神经模型，适用于非平稳数据流的持续学习，通过结构操作和现实门控实现自适应。在金融交易中，该模型可能用于捕捉市场机制变化或突发波动，动态调整模型结构以适应新市场环境，从而在多变市场中发现潜在阿尔法信号。

title: TRACE-CASH: Trial-History-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Configuration Exploration in Time-Series CASH
summary: Combined algorithm selection and hyperparameter optimization (CASH) searches a conditional space in which the selected model determines which hyperparameters are active. In time-series forecasting, temporal choices, chronological validation, and costly evaluations further complicate this search. Controlled comparisons of heterogeneous search methods under a shared time-series CASH (TS-CASH) evaluation protocol remain limited. Within this setting, we study TRACECASH, a task-local hybrid sequential optimizer combining grouped actor-critic candidate generation with fixed rules for model coverage, validation-guided exploitation, and exploration after stalled progress. A model actor proposes an initial forecasting model; three model-conditioned actors generate temporal, architectural, and training actions; and a modelspecific decoder constructs the configuration ultimately evaluated. We compare TRACE-CASH with six alternatives spanning random, Bayesian, evolutionary, multi-objective, and language-model-assisted search across 41 dataset-frequency task variants. TRACE-CASH has the lowest mean rank on both MASE and WQL. Descriptively, it also has the lowest window-averaged test-MASE rank in the predefined full and late windows. These results support the complete TRACECASH procedure as competitive among the evaluated methods.
core_methodology: TRACE-CASH combines grouped actor-critic candidate generation with fixed rules for model coverage, validation-guided exploitation, and exploration after stalled progress. It uses a model actor to propose forecasting models and model-conditioned actors to generate temporal, architectural, and training actions.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method on 41 dataset-frequency task variants, suggesting it's applicable to diverse time-series forecasting tasks, which could include financial time series.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to adaptively configure models for time-series forecasting could potentially be applied to financial market predictions, such as price or volatility forecasting, by optimizing model selection and hyperparameters dynamically.
